newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish refinery mulls up to 400 stations in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish refinery mulls up to 400 stations in 1997.

text.p: Polish oil refinery Petrochemia Plock SA, slated for partial sell-off, plans to increase the number of its filling stations to up to 400 from the current 200, the firm's deputy head said on Monday.

"The number of stations connected to us by equity links or franchise agreement is now 200...We want to increase it to between 250 and 400 by the end of the year," Marek Mroczkowski told a news briefing.
Mroczkowski also said he saw Plock's 1997 net profit at between 350 and 400 million zlotys, up from 210 million zlotys last year.
Mroczkowski, who earlier forecast the company's net at 300 million zlotys, said a better financial result would be possible thanks to the liberalisation of fuel prices in Poland earlier this year.
He said that within several weeks Plock would buy private fuel distributor Solo, which has nine stations and owns more than 10 plots of land suitable for the construction of stations.
Under a government plan to privatise the oil sector, a minority stake in Plock is to be offered to a strategic investor, most likely next year.
The investor, which would later be allowed to increase the equity to a controlling stake, would also be offered access to one-third of 1,400 petrol stations now belonging to state-own CPN company.

Plock's president Konrad Jaskola said that his company would need some 2,800 stations to distribute 8.6 million tonnes of fuels it would produce after completing its modernisation programme, probably in 1999.
